title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code Mods (Oct 1) and Claude Code 2.1.288 (Oct 2): small TypeScript functions that rewrite prompts, change UI or replace built-ins, distributed inside plugins
bullets.summary: Mods ship with 2.1.287; 2.1.288 adds reliability fixes for mid-response API timeouts and session recovery.
bullets.how: The Construct: package agent-specific behaviors (guardrails, prompt rewrites, status panes) as plugin mods instead of ad-hoc config; the timeout/session-recovery fixes help long scheduled runs. PRAGMA: a distributable customization layer for client Claude Code setups. Brand 9: no direct use.

bullets.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28): near-Opus 5.5 performance at about half the per-token cost
bullets.summary: Reported AAII score of 56, on par with Opus 5.5, available across the API and major clouds.
bullets.how: The Construct: default scheduled/routine agents to Sonnet 5.5 and reserve Opus for hard planning, cutting daily-run cost. PRAGMA: cheaper tier for client agent pilots.

bullets.title: Anthropic Claude Frontier Academy (Oct 2): $100M program to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by end of 2027
bullets.summary: Medical-residency-style training with initial cohorts from Accenture, McKinsey and Deloitte.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: validates the AI-operator consulting category and signals large incumbents will be competing for deployment talent; positioning should lean on vertical depth (signage) over generic deployment. Not relevant to Brand 9 directly.

bullets.title: Google Gemini 4 Argon begins limited rollout (Oct 1) plus new Gemini Skills for automating repetitive cross-app tasks
bullets.summary: Argon is going first to trusted cyber defenders with no GA date; reports note internal skepticism about its coding performance. Gemini Skills mirrors the skills pattern already used in Claude.
bullets.how: The Construct: skills are becoming a cross-vendor primitive, so keep our skill files portable and vendor-neutral. PRAGMA: watch for GA before benchmarking.

bullets.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol (Sep 29) and the always-on 'Dots' agent (Oct 1 DevDay)
bullets.summary: Sol reportedly matches GPT-6 Astra (71.9% DeepSWE, 71.4% OSWorld) at $2/$10 per 1M tokens; Dots is a 24/7 agent integrating with thousands of apps.
bullets.how: The Construct: benchmark Sol as a cheaper fallback for computer-use and coding agents; Dots is the consumer-grade version of our persistent-agent pattern. PRAGMA: client expectation of always-on agents is now set by OpenAI.

praxis_lesson: Skills, mods and always-on agents are now first-class primitives at Anthropic, Google and OpenAI alike, so the differentiator is no longer the harness but the governed skills, permissions and evals you own. Keep those portable and put the cheapest capable model (Sonnet 5.5) on routine runs.
